title: 2020 AMC 12B Problem 4
statement: The acute angles of a right triangle are \(a^\circ\) and \(b^\circ,\) where \(a \gt b\) and both \(a\) and \(b\) are prime numbers. What is the least possible value of \(b?\)

solutions.text:
Since the angles are complementary, \(a + b = 90.\) To minimize \(b,\) try small primes and require \(90 - b\) to be prime as well.

For \(b = 2, 3, 5,\) the value \(90 - b = 88, 87, 85\) is not prime. For \(b = 7,\) we get \(90 - 7 = 83,\) which is prime. So the least possible value is \(b = 7.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Try the smallest primes for \(b\) and check whether \(90 - b\) is also prime
